text:
maria: Hi team, PR #4823 (migration: retry/backoff doc) is blocked by a review comment asking for a definitive statement about who performs retries (server vs client) and the SDK defaults. I didn't want to guess. @kevin @tom can you confirm?

kevin: Short answer: hosted API itself does not auto-retry application requests. Retry behaviour lives in client libraries. Current defaults (runtime v2.3 era): JS SDK defaults to 3 attempts (exp backoff starting 200ms, cap 2s). Python SDK defaults to 4 attempts (exp backoff starting 150ms, cap 2.5s). Recommend callers set Idempotency-Key for safe retries on non-streaming generation endpoints.

maria: thanks. Could you post a tiny snippet for the migration guide (both showing config and Idempotency-Key usage)?

kevin: pasted JS snippet below for the docs: 

```js
// Configure JS SDK explicit retry/backoff values
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  retries: 3,
  backoffMs: 200,
  maxBackoffMs: 2000,
});

// Use Idempotency-Key on non-streaming endpoints to make retries safe
await client.generate({ prompt: '...', headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'migration-xyz-001' } });
```

maria: good. One more: does Idempotency-Key work for streaming endpoints?

kevin: No. Streaming endpoints are not retry-safe and ignore Idempotency-Key at the protocol level. Add a clear callout: "Idempotency-Key only applies to non-streaming synchronous generation endpoints."

tom: CI note 12: docs preview linkcheck flagged a cross-link to /runtime-internals which is internal-only. We need either to swap to the public serving doc or inline a brief explanation and keep the private reference under a dev-only note. @sasha any preference?

sasha: swap to public "serving-behavior" if it covers retries; otherwise inline 2-3 lines describing server-side behavior and mark the deeper runtime details as internal-only. Do NOT leave a public link to private content.

maria: I updated the PR: replaced the link with a short inline paragraph explaining that hosted API does not do automatic app-level retries and that SDKs implement client-side retry/backoff. Left an "internal: runtime details" pointer in a dev-only note. Pushed.

doc-preview-bot: Preview build available 12 2 https://deploy-preview.redwood.dev/docs/pr-4823 2 - build OK, accessibility OK, linkcheck: 1 warning (removed private link).

maria: Proposed wording for the user-facing section: 
"Redwood hosted endpoints do not automatically retry application-level requests. Client SDKs provide retry logic with exponential backoff (JS default: 3 attempts, backoff starts at ~200ms; Python default: 4 attempts, backoff starts at ~150ms). To safely retry requests, include an Idempotency-Key header for non-streaming generation endpoints. Streaming endpoints are not retry-safe and do not honor Idempotency-Key."

kevin: tiny wording tweak: add parentheses with the max backoff caps (JS 2s, Python 2.5s). Otherwise LGTM.

maria: done. I also added a short footnote about proxies/timeouts: long-lived proxies may cut connections earlier than SDK backoff windows; we suggest lowering maxBackoff when operating behind aggressive proxies.

ci-bot: docs preview succeeded; linkcheck cleared; no failing CI jobs.

tom: I can review and approve in ~20m. Looks clear, thanks. Will check the wording around idempotency and streaming again before approving.

maria: thank you all 14 marking this thread as resolved for docs blockers; leaving open for the formal review/merge step. If reviewers spot additional edge cases (batching, multipart requests), flag here.

kevin: one more note for the migration guide footnote: callers doing bulk batching should ensure idempotency semantics per item; SDK batch helpers do not automatically apply a single Idempotency-Key across multiple independent items.

maria: added that note. All set from docs side.

(End of thread)
